### Save a readable feedback sheet

```bash
canvaspilot export-feedback 41 902 --out feedback.html
```

Save the selected assignment's self-submission feedback as one HTML file you can
open locally or print. The sheet keeps reported grades beside their attempt
context, including a prominent warning when grading preceded a resubmission.
Rubric criteria retain their returned order and assessments; unmatched entries
stay separate. Comments keep supplied author names, timestamps and literal text,
including media-only entries. Attachment names and media identifiers are listed
when returned; their contents remain in Canvas.

The export uses the same reader and authentication as `feedback`. It distinguishes
zero, unknown values and explicitly empty feedback. Rubric point visibility and
rubric total visibility are applied separately, without changing the separately
reported submission grade. It calculates no grade or rubric total.

Choose a new output path: existing files, directories and symlinks are protected,
including a destination created while the feedback is being read. The completed
file contains its own styling, no scripts or automatic network resources, and
does not refresh. See [the feedback export guide](docs/feedback-export.md) for the
file's contents, exact display rules, local-file behavior and Python usage.

feedback_export = sub.add_parser(
        "export-feedback", help="Save self submission feedback to a new local HTML file",
    )
    add_common(feedback_export)
    feedback_export.add_argument("course_id", type=_positive_int)
    feedback_export.add_argument("assignment_id", type=_positive_int)
    feedback_export.add_argument("--out", required=True, type=Path,
                                 help="New HTML file; existing paths are protected")

+### Read a discussion
+
+After choosing a topic with `canvaspilot discussions <course_id>`, open it with
+`canvaspilot discussion <course_id> <topic_id>`. Add `--unread-only` to keep known
+unread replies together with their parent context. The same report is available
+through `CanvasAPI.discussion_thread()` and `canvas_discussion_thread` in MCP.
+
+The report keeps original entry fields and the returned reply structure, alongside
+cleaned text, unambiguous author attribution and reported read markers. Missing
+facts remain unknown; absent or ambiguous unread metadata does not become a
+false empty result. Canvas's cached-view boundary and unmatched unread identifiers
+remain visible. See [the discussion reader guide](docs/DISCUSSIONS.md) for fields,
+selection rules and error behavior.
+

+## Review your inbox
+
+```bash
+canvaspilot inbox --scope unread
+canvaspilot conversation 901
+```
+
+List your conversations and select a returned ID to inspect its messages.
+The CLI, Python API and existing MCP conversation reader explicitly preserve
+unread state. Original message, participant and attachment metadata are returned;
+linked content is not downloaded. See [inbox review](docs/inbox-review.md) for
+scope choices, pagination and error behavior.
